title: The architect decides meaning only; realization is the lead's; intent, priority and release are the operator's
situation: The operator and architect, 2026-10-13, reasoning from first principles about how the architect drifted: the architect's purpose was always meaning, but its recorded rights also gave it check rulings and realization decisions (0002, 0052), and the freeze made it the only one to change checks, so realization detail and mechanical work reached it constantly. A 'constraint on realization' was the exception through which gates and mechanisms were designed; tested, every such constraint is either meaning (something users see or rely on), realization (how it is built) or release.
decision: (1) The architect decides meaning only: concepts, examples, meaning questions, a cut's scope and the name of its branch, and accepting that a cut realized its meaning; it decides nothing about how anything is built. (2) The lead owns realization: the checks that bind the examples, every technical decision, which it records as a realization decision, checking out a cut's branch, and merging the cut into the project. (3) The operator decides intent, priorities, push and release. A technical requirement of the operator's is part of intent: it is recorded as the operator's decision, accepted, and binds the lead. A technical recommendation of the operator's is recorded as the operator's decision, left open, and the lead settles it by accepting it or recording its own decision with its reason. (4) The freeze: only the architect changes a cut's examples and concepts while it is built; its checks are the lead's and the check-writer's. This supersedes 0052, and 0002 and 0081 where they give the architect realization, check rulings or the checkout of a branch.
consequences: The architect, lead, decision rights, freeze, cut and decision concepts are superseded to match; the agent definitions are updated by one builder as a mechanical change, checked and reviewed by pull request.
